title: Goals vs subagents: asynchronous supervision vs synchronous fork/join
summary: Current implementation, not a proposal. Read the two numbered flows independently. GOAL: one durable objective owns a foreground coordinator Task and multiple private child Tasks. start_task returns a child record without waiting for completion; the coordinator can keep working, steer children, resolve their interactions, and explicitly wait for ordered events. SUBAGENTS: a Task calls use_subagents; the tool runs several SubagentRunner instances concurrently and returns only after the batch settles. Synchronous means the parent is awaiting the tool result, not that the agents run sequentially. Both mechanisms use the same workspace: separate conversations are not separate files or worktrees. They compose: a Goal coordinator or child Task can itself use subagents when enabled. Click nodes and edges for implementation details and source links.

nodes.label: A. GOAL — durable, asynchronous task supervision
nodes.description: A Goal is lifecycle state plus a coordinator Task, not a different kind of LLM engine. Private children are full Task instances. Goal execution and child Tasks use Act mode.

nodes.label: GoalController + GoalLoop
nodes.description: GoalController owns foreground selection; GoalLoop owns one coordinator and its child host. It constructs/reconstructs the coordinator, pins the durable objective and active-child summary into context, and owns lifecycle transitions. States: working, waiting, paused, blocked, achieved, stopped. Pause/stop abort owned execution and settle children. Recovery pauses interrupted execution and marks nonterminal children interrupted; it does not automatically restart those workers. Explicit resume reconstructs the coordinator from history. An achieved Goal cannot resume; a follow-up turn can run without changing the durable lifecycle.

nodes.label: 1. Foreground coordinator Task
nodes.description: An ordinary Task with the goal_coordinator execution profile. Receives the objective and user steering, can work directly, and is the only Goal agent communicating with the end user. Gives each child a complete self-contained assignment. After starting workers it can take more actions; it is not automatically blocked waiting for them. It synthesizes private child updates rather than mechanically forwarding them.

nodes.label: 2. GoalTaskHost — start & supervise
nodes.description: Owns the live-child registry, pending interactions, and ordered event delivery. Goal tools reach it through IToolEnvironment.goal / IGoalTrait, wired by GoalCoordinatorToolEnvironment and GoalLoop. start_task creates a durable child record, constructs a full Task through GoalTaskFactory, starts its run, and observes settlement asynchronously. Other tools list Tasks, read transcripts, send steering, cancel Tasks, resolve interactions, and wait for events. verify_goal uses the same start path with role verification.

nodes.label: 3a. Child Task A — independent loop
nodes.description: A new Task ID, conversation, TaskState, and normal Task execution loop. Starts from the supplied assignment, not a copy of the coordinator's conversation. Runs privately in Act mode. GoalChildToolEnvironment records respond progress/completion and captures questions/approvals for the host. The child cannot spawn Goal Tasks, but can call use_subagents when enabled. It shares the workspace with the coordinator and other workers.

nodes.label: 3b. Child Task B — runs concurrently
nodes.description: Another full private Task, not a serial step after A. Children can finish, fail, be cancelled, be interrupted, or wait for an interaction independently. A verify_goal call creates a child through this same mechanism with a verification assignment containing the durable objective and child-status summary. No automatic filesystem or worktree isolation is created by this path.

nodes.label: Durable objective, children & events
nodes.description: GoalStore persists the objective and its revision, lifecycle, child records, sequenced events, wake metadata, and accounting. Full Task conversations are persisted separately. Responses are recorded durably before their events are published. wait_for_goal_events claims an ordered event batch; delivery is acknowledged only once the coordinator conversation persists it. This supports recovery without treating transient in-memory workers as resumable background processes.

nodes.label: B. SUBAGENTS — parallel work inside one awaited tool call
nodes.description: Structured fork/join inside a Task. SubagentRunner is a dedicated API/tool loop, not a new full Task. Sibling runners execute concurrently; the parent waits for their batch to settle.

nodes.label: 1. Parent Task — awaits tool result
nodes.description: May be a standalone Task, Goal coordinator, or Goal child when subagents are enabled. Calls use_subagents with a list of assignments. Its next model step depends on the aggregate tool result; it does not get a Goal-style registry of independently steerable subagent Tasks. Progress cards can update while the model is waiting. Cancelling the parent propagates to the runners.

nodes.label: 2. use_subagents — fork the batch
nodes.description: Validates requests, allocates agent identities, and creates aggregate/per-agent cards. Uses requests.map(async ...) to start one execution per request. Each execution calls env.orchestration.runSubagent; OrchestrationTraitBuilder constructs SubagentRunner and connects cancellation, progress, recording, and usage accounting. The tool owns this entire batch lifecycle. Recursive subagent spawning is rejected.

nodes.label: 3a. SubagentRunner A — LLM ⇄ tools
nodes.description: Own API handler/runtime, local conversation, fresh TaskState, and scoped tool dispatcher; NOT new Task(...). Inherits the parent's task identity, workspace and mode through TaskConfig. Starts with its prompt and workspace metadata; include_history optionally seeds its conversation with the parent's API history. Builds its own prompt/tool snapshot. SubagentToolExecutor intercepts respond complete to end this run; other permitted tools dispatch through the normal tool infrastructure.

nodes.label: 3b. SubagentRunner B — runs concurrently
nodes.description: Same execution structure as A, with separate local conversation/state and provider runtime. Default work deadline is 600 seconds, configurable per request. Deadline expiry enters wrap-up, disallows further task work, and allows up to 90 seconds to report completion before termination. Parent cancellation aborts the run. No nested subagents. Sibling failure does not short-circuit Promise.allSettled for the rest of the batch.

nodes.label: 4. Join all → aggregate tool result
nodes.description: This is the join phase inside UseSubagentsTool, not a separate service. await Promise.allSettled(execution) waits for all executions, reconciles each success/failure/cancellation and usage, finalizes presentation, and formats a combined result. The parent model then continues with that tool result. Subagent completion ends only that runner, not the parent Task.

nodes.label: Live cards + parent-owned run artifacts
nodes.description: Progress/tool trajectory/usage updates feed the aggregate and per-agent cards while the parent awaits. SubagentRunRecorder writes transcript.md and diagnostics.md under the parent task directory at subagents/<runId>/, with an index.md. Usage is published into the parent message state. These are observable run artifacts, not independent resumable Task records; recorder/presentation failures are logged rather than defining the execution result.

nodes.label: Shared workspace — not isolated worktrees
nodes.description: GoalTaskFactory passes the same cwd/workspace manager into its Tasks; SubagentRunner derives its config from the parent. Both mechanisms separate conversation/execution state, but neither path automatically isolates filesystem changes. Concurrent assignments must avoid conflicting edits, and writes made before a failure/cancellation are not automatically rolled back by these mechanisms.

edges.label: start_task → immediate child record
edges.description: Via StartTaskTool → IToolEnvironment.goal → GoalLoop's IGoalTrait binding → GoalTaskHost. Waits for startup, not for the child's run to complete. The coordinator can keep acting after the record is returned.

edges.label: steer / inspect / resolve / cancel
edges.description: send_task_message injects steering into a live child; read_task_transcript and list_tasks inspect it. resolve_task_interaction can answer/allow/reject or relay an interaction to the user through the coordinator.

edges.label: start another Task without joining A
private progress / questions / outcome
edges.description: GoalChildToolEnvironment observes responses and captures interactions; observeRun records terminal outcomes. These become host-managed events, not direct user messages.

edges.label: pin objective + active-child summary
edges.description: GoalLoop.pinnedContext supplies current durable context to the coordinator.

edges.label: 4. wait_for_goal_events → event batch
edges.description: Explicit wait returns queued responses, interactions, failures, completions or steering in sequence, plus active-task status. The coordinator reasons about what to do next; children do not automatically suspend/resume the model on every update.

edges.label: 5. complete → no-live-child guard → achieved
edges.description: GoalLoop.commitCompletion uses GoalTaskHost.commitTerminalAttempt to reject completion while any child is active. Only successful completion of active Goal pursuit requests achieved; a follow-up completion ends just that turn.

edges.label: env.orchestration.runSubagent(prompt A)
edges.description: The tool uses IToolEnvironment; OrchestrationTraitBuilder creates and runs the SubagentRunner.
